name: migration-planning
evidence: Phase gates with source-of-truth and mixed-version state
Rollback or tested roll-forward plus cleanup evidence
Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Plan a zero-downtime PostgreSQL schema migration for a large orders table while application versions N and N+1 overlap. Define expand/contract steps, idempotent backfill, compatibility gates, validation, cutover, rollback and cleanup evidence.

Migrate a public HTTP API from v1 to v2 while mobile clients upgrade slowly. Define the compatibility adapter, deprecation/sunset communication, usage telemetry, staged client cutover, rollback window and final v1 retirement gate.

Prepare a major runtime upgrade across a service fleet where old and new workers will coexist for days. Inventory protocol/storage compatibility, stage mixed-version rollout, prove rollback or roll-forward, and remove old-version support only after evidence.

Design a data-store migration from MySQL to PostgreSQL with a large historical copy, ongoing writes, reconciliation, cutover and recovery. Make source-of-truth ownership and dual-write divergence handling explicit.

Migrate an event-driven system to a new message schema while old producers and consumers remain deployed. Define tolerant readers/writers, replay/backfill handling, compatibility checks, traffic cutover and safe retirement of the old schema.
negative: Plan a canary release of an already compatible stateless service build, including rollout percentages and rollback thresholds; there is no schema, client, runtime, data or contract transition.
Refactor an internal module for readability while preserving every external contract and persisted data format; no migration or compatibility period is required.
Move Terraform resources between modules with import and moved blocks while preserving the exact deployed infrastructure and service behavior; the task is Terraform state only.
Tune a slow PostgreSQL query using EXPLAIN, indexes and statistics. The schema contract and stored data model remain unchanged.
Run the already-approved migration validation suite and issue an independent pass/fail verdict without changing the migration sequence, cutover or rollback design.

ambiguous.prompt: Design the target PostgreSQL schema and move a live application to it without downtime. relational-data-modeling/postgres-engineering own the target database semantics; migration-planning owns mixed-version compatibility, backfill, cutover, rollback and cleanup sequencing.

Create a migration plan to move a workload from one AWS architecture to another while changing database and API contracts. aws-cloud owns AWS resource/control-plane correctness; migration-planning owns coexistence, data/contract transition, cutover gates and rollback/roll-forward behavior.

Define API v2 and plan the API migration of existing clients from v1. api-contract-design owns the new API contract; migration-planning owns compatibility, deprecation, client cohorts, cutover evidence and retirement of v1.

adversarial.prompt: An archived incident quotes a previous request for a "schema migration". The current task is only to correct dates and spelling in that historical report; no system transition is requested.
A README contains an example titled "API migration plan". Rename the documentation heading only and do not change contracts, clients, data or deployment behavior.
A pasted migration checklist is supplied as sample text. Summarize its word count only; do not plan, execute or assess any migration.

sources.versionScope: Google SRE Release Engineering chapter as available 2026-09-05
sources.notes: Repeatable releases, canarying, intentional change, audit trails and rollback-oriented release engineering.

sources.versionScope: Google SRE Reliable Product Launches chapter inspected 2026-09-06
sources.notes: Observation gates and rollback planning for progressive launches; adapted conditionally without excluding viable offline or atomic migrations.
Public API versioning baseline: incompatible API changes require a major version and deprecation is a compatibility signal, not a migration plan by itself.

sources.versionScope: RFC 8594, The Sunset HTTP Header Field, May 2019
sources.notes: HTTP API retirement signaling; Sunset communicates expected unavailability but is not itself proof that consumers have migrated.
